name: Water
where: The stream and the lake. Dip an open container in.
desc: Clear, tasteless and the most useful solvent there is.

name: Salt
where: The kitchen at home, and pink rock salt in the cave.
desc: Sodium chloride. Dissolves easily and conducts electricity in water.

name: Baking soda
desc: Sodium bicarbonate. Fizzes with acid; turns into washing soda when heated.

name: Vinegar
desc: About 5% acetic acid in water. A weak acid.

name: Sugar
desc: Sucrose. Caramelises when heated, then chars to carbon.

name: Quartz sand
where: Sandy banks of the stream and the lake beach.
desc: Silicon dioxide. The main ingredient of glass.

name: Limestone
where: The pale outcrop beside the lake.
desc: Calcium carbonate. Fizzes in acid; turns into quicklime in great heat.

name: Hematite (iron ore)
where: The rusty red rocks east of the lab.
desc: Iron oxide. Smelt it with charcoal to get iron.

name: Malachite (copper ore)
where: The green-streaked rocks north-west of the lab, near the cave.
desc: A green copper mineral. Roast it, then smelt it with charcoal.

name: Native copper
desc: Pure copper metal that formed naturally in rock.

name: Gold flakes
desc: Gold does not react with water or air, so it lies in streams as pure metal.

name: Meteorite iron
where: A small crater in the far south of the forest.
desc: Iron and nickel that fell from space. Ancient people made tools from it.

name: Sulfur crystals
where: Around the warm vent in the cave.
desc: Yellow crystals left by volcanic gases. Burns with a blue flame.

name: Coal
where: The black seam in the cave wall.
desc: Ancient plants turned to carbon. Burns hot.

name: Charcoal
where: The old campfire south of the lab.
desc: Wood heated without much air. Nearly pure carbon.

name: Quartz crystal
where: The glittering wall in the cave.
desc: Silicon dioxide grown as clear crystals.

name: Elderberries
where: Dark bushes on the lake shore.
desc: Full of anthocyanin dye. Crush in water for a natural pH indicator.
